Campbell County by the numbers

Which Campbell County offices touch a Northern Kentucky tax bill?

Three offices share a Campbell bill. The Property Valuation Administrator sets the value, the Sheriff's Office mails and collects, and the County Clerk inherits what goes delinquent. Rates come from neither the PVA nor the sheriff: the PVA's page explains that every taxing district's board figures its rate from the assessments inside that district.

The county runs along the Ohio and Licking Rivers and has two seats, Newport and Alexandria, with sheriff's windows in each. At 93,076 residents in 2020 and 615 people per square mile, Campbell is the densest county in this group by a wide margin, and it has the highest home values.

By law the PVA assesses at 100 percent of fair market value, meaning the price a willing buyer and seller would agree on. Field staff look at every parcel in person at least every four years, and new construction is reviewed when it appears.

History explains the two offices. Campbell was formed on December 17, 1794 as Kentucky's 19th county, and an 1883 law let Newport keep a separate court house district while Alexandria remained the legal seat until a 2010 ruling gave Newport equal status. The county is the fourth-smallest in Kentucky by land and has six school districts, so which district serves a house changes the school line on the bill.

Rates move each year under House Bill 44. A district can adopt the compensating rate, which keeps revenue from existing property flat as values rise, or a rate that raises up to 4 percent more, which needs a public hearing. A rate above that can be put to a recall vote. A rise in your assessed value therefore does not automatically mean a bigger bill.

What is the Campbell County payment calendar?

The PVA's calendar has finished bills reaching the sheriff by September 15, and mailing usually follows around November 1. For 2025 the sheriff ran the discount phase from November 1 through November 30, which the PVA's calendar phrases as payment with discount before December 1.

  • All of December: face amount, no discount.
  • All of January: delinquent, plus 5 percent.
  • From February 1: plus 10 percent and a 10 percent sheriff's add-on fee.
  • Older years: settled at the County Clerk, never the sheriff.

One line item surprises owners: the 911 fee printed on the bill is exempt from the 2% discount and stays at full price. The sheriff mails only to the listed owner and cannot redirect a bill to a lender, so anyone with escrow should pass the bill along at once.

Which payment options does the Campbell sheriff offer?

Owners can pay online, by mail, or at either sheriff's location. Newport's office sits in the County Administration Building at 1098 Monmouth Street, and Alexandria's is at 8330 West Main Street. The sheriff's tax page lists weekday hours from 8 in the morning until 4 in the afternoon at both.

The web option goes through an outside vendor. A card payment adds a 3 percent charge to the cardholder, an e-check adds $3, and e-checks above $30,000 are refused. The sheriff keeps none of those fees. A mailed check should name the sheriff and show the bill number, and the canceled check is your receipt.

A returned check puts the bill back to unpaid on the sheriff's and PVA's records, and the repayment must follow the schedule printed on the bill. That matters in a closing week, when a bounced check can leave a lien open.

How does a Campbell County appeal work?

A PVA conference has to happen before the 13-day inspection period ends, and the appeal itself is filed with the county. Inspection starts the first Monday in May, per the PVA's calendar, and the Board of Assessment Appeals then meets for five days starting 25 to 35 days after it closes.

The state calendar sets the filing deadline at the workday after inspection ends, while the county PVA's calendar lists six work days. With the two sources differing, read the dates on your notice and get the exact last day from the PVA before filing. Anyone paid to represent you must be an attorney, appraiser, accountant, licensed broker or similar professional under KRS 133.120.

Good evidence for a Newport or Alexandria house includes recent sales of similar homes, photos of damage and repair estimates. The state revenue guide adds that the PVA should be able to hand over the sales used to value your home, so request that list first.

Which exemptions and corrections can Campbell County owners request?

Owners who reach 65, or who are totally disabled, can apply for a homestead or disability exemption through the PVA, which can state the filing cutoff for the year. The state wants disability verification before December 31. The sheriff's page advises owners turning 65 to contact the PVA before paying.

The PVA at 1098 Monmouth Street, (859) 292-3871, also fixes a wrong property address, mailing address or owner name. Corrections can be written on the return stub, which the sheriff forwards. An assessment or exemption can be changed only by the PVA.

  • PVA, 1098 Monmouth Street: value, address, name and exemption questions.
  • Sheriff, Newport or Alexandria: bill lookup and payment.
  • County Clerk, (859) 292-3845: any year that has gone delinquent.

Farm acreage is valued at its agricultural value, which the state's assessment guide says can sit far below the market price per acre in urban areas. A seller with a few acres at the edge of Alexandria should ask the PVA how the parcel is classed.

What happens to Campbell County taxes when I sell?

The debt travels with the parcel, so the title company will want a payoff of the current bill and any delinquent certificate before closing. KRS 134.015 makes the tax a personal debt of the owner on the January 1 assessment date, and the delinquency lien continues under KRS 134.420 no matter who owns the house afterward.

A bill that outlasts the sheriff's season moves to the County Clerk carrying a 10 percent penalty, the sheriff's fee and 1 percent monthly interest. Clerk, county attorney and third-party purchaser fees pile on from there, and the state's collection page works five examples, running from about $1,388 to $1,704 on a $1,000 bill. The clerk at (859) 292-3845 gives the live figure.

An owner who has fallen behind can still sell as-is, with the payoff deducted from proceeds. Early numbers from the clerk show what remains.

How strong is the Campbell County housing market?

Home values here lead this group: $252,000 is the 2020 to 2024 median for owner-occupied homes, and 182 building permits were issued in 2025. The county belongs to the Cincinnati metropolitan area, and Northern Kentucky University is in Highland Heights.

Campbell County housing profile from the Census Bureau's QuickFacts page
ItemValue
Residents (2025 estimate)95,441
Homes counted in mid-202543,090
Share lived in by owners71.1%
Typical home value$252,000
Typical monthly rent$1,145
Typical monthly owner cost, mortgaged$1,627

Only 86.1 percent of residents lived at the same address a year earlier, the lowest of the four counties, which points to more moves and more rentals. Owners of older Newport homes, duplexes or inherited houses can sell directly for cash when repairs or tenants slow a standard listing.

More questions about Campbell County, KY Property Tax Guide

When do Campbell County tax bills go out?

Mailing typically happens around November 1. In 2025 the 2% discount lasted through November 30, December was face value, January added 5%, and after January 31 a 10% penalty and sheriff's fee applied.

Where do I take a Campbell County payment?

Visit the Sheriff's Office in Newport (1098 Monmouth Street) or Alexandria (8330 West Main Street), mail it, or use the vendor link on the sheriff's tax page.

Is the 911 fee discounted?

No. The sheriff states that the 911 line on a bill is outside the 2% discount.

Who handles questions about my Campbell value?

The PVA, at (859) 292-3871. The sheriff only collects, and cannot alter an assessment, address or exemption.

Can a house with unpaid Campbell taxes still sell?

Yes. Delinquent bills sit with the County Clerk, and closing pays them from the proceeds. Ask the clerk, at (859) 292-3845, for the amount before fixing a date.

Daviess County by the numbers

What kind of housing market does Daviess County have?

Daviess County is western Kentucky's river-city market. Owensboro anchors it, and the Census Bureau places the county in the Owensboro metropolitan area on the Ohio River. Kentucky cut it from Ohio County on January 14, 1815. The name carries an old typo: the man it honors, Joseph Hamilton Daveiss, was entered with the wrong spelling in the state clerk's records, and the error stuck.

The county spans 477 square miles, 18 of them water. Land along the river in the north is mostly level, while the south rolls into hills and valleys that once supplied coal near Panther Creek. Residents numbered 103,312 in 2020, and the July 2025 estimate of 104,898 is 1.5 percent higher.

What do Census figures say about Daviess County homes?

QuickFacts for the 2020 to 2024 period and 2025 show a market with real depth:

  • 45,155 housing units across 41,639 households
  • 68.1 percent of households own, so close to a third rent
  • Typical home value: $199,900
  • Typical rent: $918 a month
  • Typical monthly owner cost: $1,387 with a mortgage, $512 without
  • 253 building permits in 2025

Apply the Fiscal Court's real property rate of 12.2 cents per $100 to a $199,900 house and the county's own share comes to roughly $244 a year. School, city and special district rates sit on top of that.

Who sends and collects the Daviess County bill?

The Sheriff's Office tax division handles both, at 212 St. Ann Street, Room 103, in Owensboro. The counter takes questions at 270-685-6133 on weekdays until 4:30. It closes for Veterans Day, Thanksgiving, Black Friday, Christmas Eve, Christmas Day, New Year's Eve and New Year's Day.

Mailing happens during the first week of November. A homeowner whose lender pays from escrow may still receive a bill, because the servicer sometimes intends to pay without asking the sheriff to hold a copy. If you expect a bill and see none, allow a couple of days for postal delays, then look the parcel up on the sheriff's website, since the mailing address on file may be wrong. Call or email the tax counter with the parcel numbers to correct an address. Property inside Owensboro also owes city tax through the City of Owensboro Tax Office at 270-687-8537.

What did Daviess County set as its tax rates for 2025?

In August 2025 the Fiscal Court adopted the compensating rate for real property, dropping the county's figure from 12.9 cents to 12.2 cents per $100 of assessed value. Tangible personal property stayed at 13.8 cents, and motor vehicles and watercraft at 17 cents. The county called it its biggest tax cut in at least twenty years.

These are the county's rates alone. School districts and other taxing bodies add their own, which makes a parcel's full rate higher than 12.2 cents. Ask the tax counter for a parcel-level bill, or search the parcel on the sheriff's website, before telling a buyer what the house will cost to carry.

What are the Daviess County payment windows?

The Department of Revenue approved a calendar that repeats each year. A payment inside the first window saves 2 percent, and each later window costs more.

Daviess County collection periods (source: Daviess County Sheriff's Office, Tax Collection page)
WindowEffect
November 10 to December 102 percent discount
December 11 to January 10Base amount
January 11 to February 105 percent penalty
February 11 to April 2521 percent penalty

Under KRS 134.119, a mailed payment with a U.S. Postal Service postmark inside the window is on time. A returned check costs $25, and the bill goes back to unpaid.

How can I pay a Daviess County property tax bill?

Three channels work. Online, go to dcsoky.gov and use Pay Taxes Online. Several bills can share a cart, the options are card or electronic check, and the fee appears before you confirm. The office warns that payments sent through any other website will not be honored.

  • At the counter: cash, card, check, cashier's check or money order, with checks for the exact amount
  • By mail: checks payable to the Daviess County Sheriff's Office, drawn on U.S. banks only
  • Online: card or e-check on the sheriff's own site

Two bills for one parcel usually mean an exemption was added after the first printing. Read both and look up the balance online.

How do I challenge a Daviess County assessment?

Call the PVA at 270-685-8474 first. A conference with the PVA or a deputy is required before any appeal, and it must happen inside the May inspection window, which opens the first Monday of May and lasts thirteen days. The value being tested is the January 1 fair cash value.

When the conference settles nothing, file at the County Clerk's office, 270-685-8434, by the close of the following workday. The local board of assessment appeals sits 25 to 35 days after the window ends and rules on evidence, so bring comparable sales, an appraisal or repair quotes. A board ruling you dispute can go to the Kentucky Board of Tax Appeals.

Can a Daviess County homeowner lower the taxable value?

People at least 65, or classified as totally disabled, can claim the homestead exemption on the home they occupy. For 2025 and 2026 it is worth $49,100. A house assessed at $199,900 would be taxed on $150,800.

The application goes to the Daviess County PVA. A driver's license, birth certificate or passport proves age. A disability claim needs proof that a federal agency or a retirement system classified you as totally disabled.

What if I sell a Daviess County house after bills are printed?

The sheriff's office tells anyone who sold or bought after January 1 and thinks a bill came in error to ask the closing title company. Valuation fixes on January 1 under KRS 132.220, so paperwork can trail a sale. Your settlement statement should split the year's tax between seller and buyer.

A delinquent notice goes out on February 11. When business closes on April 25, unpaid bills pass to the County Clerk, carrying heavy fees and exposure to the tax sale. A delinquency can be paid off from the sale proceeds at closing.

What does a delinquent Daviess County bill turn into?

After April 25 the bill becomes a certificate of delinquency held by the County Clerk, with a lien on the parcel. The state process adds interest at 1 percent a month, a 10 percent clerk fee and a 20 percent county attorney fee. The county attorney mails notices by mid-May and mid-June, and installments may be possible.

From mid-July to late October the clerk may sell certificates to private buyers, after advertising the list in the local paper and on the clerk's website at least 30 days ahead. Once a buyer holds the certificate, the owner pays that buyer, who adds charges. Anyone planning a sale with a delinquency should settle it before the summer sale dates.

More questions about Daviess County, KY Property Tax Guide

When does the Daviess County 2 percent discount end?

December 10 every year. The window opens November 10, and bills are mailed in the first week of November.

What is the final day to pay a Daviess County bill before it goes to the clerk?

April 25, at close of business. After that the bill moves to the County Clerk with added fees and can be offered at the tax sale.

Can I pay Daviess County property tax online?

Yes, through the Pay Taxes Online link on the Daviess County Sheriff's Office site, dcsoky.gov. Card and e-check payments carry a fee that shows before you confirm.

Who do I phone when my Daviess County value looks too high?

The PVA at 270-685-8474, to book the conference that Kentucky requires before an appeal can be filed with the County Clerk.

Does Owensboro bill its own property tax?

Yes. The City of Owensboro Tax Office, 270-687-8537, bills city tax separately from the county bill the sheriff sends.

Bullitt County by the numbers

What is Bullitt County, Kentucky, like for a home seller?

Bullitt County is the Louisville suburb that grew into a distribution hub. It sits just south of Jefferson County, with Spencer, Nelson and Hardin counties on its other sides, and covers 300 square miles in the Knobs region of the western Bluegrass. Shepherdsville is the county seat and the oldest town. Mount Washington is the largest city, and ten miles of Kentucky 44 link the two with homes along nearly the whole stretch.

Interstate 65 runs through the middle of the county. More than six million square feet of distribution and warehouse space has been built since 2000, with business parks about 16 miles from Louisville's airport and the UPS Worldport. The western fifth of the county, about 62 square miles, belongs to Fort Knox training land. UofL Health South Hospital opened in Shepherdsville in March 2024, and Bernheim Arboretum and Research Forest in Clermont is a visitor draw. The county's tourism impact was estimated at $173.2 million for 2025.

Bullitt's Lick, a salt lick near the Salt River, supplied Kentucky's first industry until around 1830, and the county was organized from parts of Jefferson and Nelson counties by an act approved December 13, 1796.

How do Bullitt County housing numbers compare?

Census QuickFacts puts the 2025 population at 86,454, up 5.1 percent from 82,224 in the April 2020 base. The housing figures run higher than in nearby rural counties:

  • Median value of owner-occupied homes: $247,200 (2020 to 2024), the highest of Boyle, Bracken, Breckinridge and Bullitt.
  • Owner-occupied rate: 84.9 percent across 31,747 households.
  • Median gross rent: $987, and median owner cost with a mortgage $1,561 a month.
  • Median household income: $80,558, with 8.5 percent of residents in poverty.
  • Building permits issued in 2025: 654, against 34,722 housing units.

The 2020 count found 31,409 households, a median age of 40.3, and 70.5 percent of residents in urban areas. Monthly owner costs in the middle are $524 for owners without a mortgage, and 93.6 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier. About 18.7 percent of residents are 65 or older, which is the group the homestead exemption serves, and 92.1 percent of households have broadband. The county counts 4,923 veterans. The mean commute is 28.7 minutes. Transportation and warehousing receipts in 2022 reached $327.8 million, which fits a county where trucking and logistics employ many residents. Density is 276.8 people per square mile.

Which Bullitt County office collects the property tax?

The Sheriff's Office takes the money and distributes it to the state, county, schools and special districts. Its office is on the first floor of the courthouse at 300 South Buckman Street in Shepherdsville, phone 502-543-2514, and it collects over $170 million a year. Mail goes to PO Box 205, Shepherdsville, KY 40165. Between October 1 and December 31 you can also pay by check at any Stock Yards Bank branch in the county.

Assessments belong to the PVA, whose county annex office is at 149 North Walnut Street, phone 502-543-7480. The County Clerk, at 502-955-6369, gives payoff figures for delinquent bills from earlier years.

What are the Bullitt County tax dates?

The sheriff receives the bills from the clerk at the end of September and most owners see them in the first week of October. The 2026 bills list four due dates, by receipt or postmark:

  • November 1: face value less a 2 percent discount.
  • December 31: face value.
  • January 31: face value plus a 5 percent penalty.
  • April 15: face value plus a 21 percent penalty.

After April 1, the sheriff no longer accepts personal or business checks. Pay with cash, a certified check, a money order or a card. Card fees are set by the processor. Partial payments are refused, and an owner who has not received a bill by mid-October should call for a duplicate.

What is the Bullitt County tax rate for 2026?

The sheriff publishes a rate chart for each jurisdiction. The chart lists these 2026 real estate rates by jurisdiction, and the state line of 10.30 matches the cents-per-$100 form Kentucky uses.

2026 Bullitt County real estate rates by jurisdiction (source: Bullitt County Sheriff)
JurisdictionReal estate rate
State10.30
County8.7
Health2.4
Library4.9
School73.10
County Extension0.90
Shepherdsville10.10
Mount Washington Fire20.0

The first six lines add up to 100.30. The Nichols, Southeast and Zoneton fire districts are each 10.0, and a Plum Creek water line of 1.0 applies to real estate in its area. Shepherdsville's own tax comes combined with the county bill. Other incorporated places, including Mount Washington, Hillview, Hunters Hollow, Pioneer Village, Fox Chase, Lebanon Junction and Hebron Estates, bill their own city tax, so call the city. The tax district code on the bill tells you which applies.

Which Bullitt County school district applies?

Bullitt County Public Schools serves nearly the whole county and accounts for the largest line on the bill at 73.10. The Department of Defense Education Activity runs the schools on Fort Knox, including Fort Knox Middle High School. The county's high schools are Bullitt Central in Shepherdsville, Bullitt East in Mount Washington, North Bullitt in Hebron Estates and Riverview. Bernheim, Bullitt Lick, Eastside, Hebron, Mount Washington and Zoneton run the middle schools.

Who gets the homestead exemption in Bullitt County?

An owner who is 65 or older on January 1 and lives in the home can reduce the assessment by up to $49,100. The sheriff's page tells owners to bring proof of age, such as a driver's license, to the PVA with the application before paying. A totally disabled owner qualifies under the state rule as well. The application goes to the PVA by December 31 of the tax year.

How does an assessment appeal work in Bullitt County?

Request a conference at the PVA once the notice arrives. The tax roll is open for inspection for thirteen days starting the first Monday in May, and a filing at the County Clerk is due the workday after the inspection period ends. The board of assessment appeals sits for as many as five days, starting 25 to 35 days after inspection closes. Bring comparable sales and photos, because the board decides on evidence and a case with none is denied.

How should a Bullitt County seller handle the tax at closing?

The bill goes to the January 1 owner. A house that sells in the spring is still billed to the seller, and the closing agent divides the year between the parties. The sheriff requires the full bill to be paid, so the settlement statement must show who pays. Anything unpaid after April 15 moves to the clerk with a lien, and interest runs 1 percent a month; ask for a payoff before the closing date. Sellers with inherited, tenant-occupied or heavily worn houses can often close with a cash buyer and have the tax paid from proceeds.

What is the Bullitt County sheriff's phone number for taxes?

Call 502-543-2514. The office is on the first floor of the courthouse at 300 South Buckman Street in Shepherdsville.

When does the Bullitt County 2% discount end?

For the 2026 bills it ends November 1, by receipt or postmark. December 31 is face value, January 31 adds 5 percent, and April 15 adds 21 percent.

Can I pay Bullitt County taxes at a bank?

Yes. Any Stock Yards Bank branch in the county takes check payments from October 1 to December 31 during business hours.

Does Shepherdsville charge a separate city tax?

No separate bill. Shepherdsville's tax is combined with the county bill, while other cities such as Mount Washington and Hillview bill their own city tax.

How much is the Bullitt County homestead exemption?

Up to $49,100 off the assessed value for owners 65 or older who live in the home on January 1. Apply at the PVA before paying the bill.

Who sets and who collects property tax in Bourbon County, Kentucky?

Two offices in the Paris courthouse building split the work. The Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) in Room 15 sets the value. The Sheriff's Office in Room 104 sends the bills and takes the money.

The county directory lists the PVA at (859) 987-2152, extension 217, and the sheriff at (859) 987-2130. Both offices open at half past eight on weekdays and close at four-thirty. The sheriff's page adds that the office shuts on holidays such as Good Friday, Memorial Day, Veterans Day and Thanksgiving.

How big is Bourbon County, and what does that mean for assessments?

Bourbon County covers roughly 290 square miles of mostly open, rolling farmland around Paris, with Millersburg and North Middletown as the smaller towns. Census figures put the population at 20,243 in 2025 and the housing stock at 9,399 units.

Home values here run well above neighboring Boyd County's $130,700 median. Typical home value is $229,300 and the owner-occupied share is 63.7%, both Census Bureau estimates. A seller with acreage can ask the PVA in Room 15 for the parcel record and compare it with a recent local sale before assuming the figure is right.

When are Bourbon County property taxes due?

The Sheriff's Office collects from November 1 through April 15. Paying sooner costs less, and the sheriff honors a U.S. postmark as the payment date.

Pay at the Sheriff's Office, 301 Main Street, Suite 104, Paris, or mail a check to that address. Bills are mailed to the homeowner as postcards, so a seller whose mortgage company pays from escrow should ask the lender whether it needs a copy.

  • Accepted: cash, cashier's checks, money orders, and personal or business checks drawn on U.S. banks.

  • Third party checks and foreign funds are refused.

Can I dispute a Bourbon County assessment?

Yes. Assessments reflect January 1, and no forms come first: you ask the PVA or a deputy for a conference.

KRS 133.120 governs the steps. Request the conference while the May inspection window is open, which is a two-week stretch that the state can lengthen for a county. Still disagree? Write to the County Clerk with your reasons and what you believe the property is worth, and the clerk routes the letter to the board of assessment appeals. The deadline is one workday after the window closes. At the hearing, bring evidence: nearby sales, an appraisal or a contractor's repair quote.

Filing never stops the bill. Pay on the value you claim. If the board lands higher, the gap is billed later with interest. Skipping the county board closes the door on the state-level Board of Tax Appeals.

Is there a homestead exemption in Bourbon County?

Applications go to the PVA in Room 15. Take a $200,000 assessment. After the deduction, tax is figured on $150,900. A disability claim is refiled every year unless the owner is a veteran with a service-connected disability or has been ruled permanently disabled by Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems. Ask the PVA which figure your bill uses, because the amount is reset every two years.

Bring the postcard bill or the parcel details, plus a payment the office accepts. Checks go out to the Bourbon County Sheriff's Office, and the sheriff's page lists the closings that matter for timing: Martin Luther King Day, Good Friday, Memorial Day, Independence Day, Labor Day, Veterans Day, Thanksgiving, Christmas and New Year's.

  • Count a mailed check as paid on its postmark date, and mail early in November to keep the discount.
  • Skip online payment: the sheriff states the office offers neither online nor phone payment.
  • Check that the check is drawn on a U.S. bank and is not made out by a third party.

What does a late Bourbon County tax bill cost in real dollars?

Take a bill of $2,000. Paid during November it is $1,960 after the 2% discount. In December it is $2,000. In January the 5% penalty makes it $2,100, and from February 1 through April 15 the 21% period brings it to $2,420. That is a $460 spread between paying in November and waiting until the last collection day.

The sheriff posts that last stretch as a 21% penalty period, and the 21% is the figure used above. What do other Bourbon County figures show about the housing market?

The county issued 109 building permits in 2025, far more than Boyd County's 12, and retail sales per person in 2022 were $39,822. Median household income was $61,354 for 2020 to 2024, and 13.9% of residents were in poverty. The Census Bureau finds 94.9% of residents in the same house they occupied a year before. Turnover is low, and listings stay few.

That steadiness helps a seller who has the paperwork in order. A buyer's lender or title company will want the current tax bill, the deed and any lien releases on the table at closing, and each of those comes from an office within one building at 301 Main Street.

What becomes of the tax bill when a Bourbon County house sells?

Unpaid tax becomes a charge on the house itself, while the debt belongs to whoever owned it on the January 1 assessment date. The closing agent will confirm the bill is current.

  • Check with the sheriff on whether this year's bill is paid and in which collection period.
  • Give the buyer's mailing address in the deed's tax-bill line so the next postcard finds them.
  • Agree with the buyer on how this year's tax is split.
  • For a past-due year, expect the clerk, not the sheriff, to quote the payoff.

December 31 is the last day for the plain face amount. The 2% discount ends November 30, and the 5% penalty begins January 1.

At the Sheriff's Office, 301 Main Street, Suite 104, Paris, or by mail to that address. Card payments are accepted only in person, with a 3.5% fee.

The sheriff passes it to the County Clerk, and the sheriff's page says significant added fees apply.

Begin with a PVA conference in May. If it fails, send the County Clerk a written petition the workday after the inspection window closes.

Owners aged 65 and up, plus owners classed as totally disabled, who file with the PVA. The state's deduction is $49,100 across 2025 and 2026.

Who sets the value and who sends the bill in Clark County, Kentucky?

Two offices do the bulk of the work. The Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) assigns each parcel its assessed value, and the sheriff mails and collects the bill starting around October 1. The county clerk steps in after April 15 for anything left unpaid. The sheriff's own page says the office never puts a value on property: your bill is the PVA's value multiplied by the rate for each taxing body covering the parcel, such as the state, the county, a school district or a special district.

The county sits next to Lexington and belongs to its metropolitan area. It covers 255 square miles, and Winchester serves as both seat and sole city. If your house is inside Winchester, ask the city whether it bills a separate city tax and when. The 2020 census counted 36,972 residents, which gives Clark a bigger and more urban tax base than the mountain counties to its east.

Where can I pay a Clark County property tax bill?

The Clark County Sheriff's Office takes payment by several routes, and its 2025 taxpayer notice laid them out. The sheriff's office is in the basement of the Governor James Clark Judicial Building in Winchester, and the phone number for questions is (859) 744-4390.

If a bill has not reached you by October 15, call the sheriff. A buyer or mortgage company that should pay it needs the bill forwarded right away.

What are the Clark County due dates and penalties?

They are the same dates every year, set by KRS 134.015 and printed in the sheriff's notice. Use them as a recurring calendar rather than a one-time list.

  • Through November 1: pay in full and take a 2 percent discount.
  • Late autumn through year end (November 2 to December 31): the bill as printed.
  • Every day in January: 5 percent is added.
  • February 1 to April 15: a 10 percent penalty plus a 10 percent add-on.

The county clerk takes over whatever is still unpaid when business closes on April 15. The sheriff's notice warns that payments at the clerk's office carry a 20 percent county attorney fee, a 10 percent clerk fee and monthly interest of 1 percent, and that delinquent bills can be sold to a third party. The county's own FAQ says the same: bills go out October 1, the face amount ends December 31, and collection passes to the clerk after April 15.

What do sellers find in Clark County?

An old settlement with in-town houses and working farms side by side. Records show settlers here as early as 1753, and the county was cut from Bourbon and Fayette in 1792. Railroads arrived in 1873 and the early 1880s, and once I-64 met the Mountain Parkway near Winchester in the 1960s, manufacturing moved in around the city.

The 2020 census found 14,917 households and 16,116 housing units. About 65.6 percent of occupied homes were owned and 34.4 percent rented, with 7.4 percent of units vacant and a median age of 41.5. The census counted about 71 percent of residents in urban areas, and the rest in rural parts of the county, where acreage and farm parcels change hands.

  • The Kentucky River, Red River, Lulbegrud Creek and Boone's Creek cross the county, so parcels near the water deserve a look at flood risk before you list.
  • Tobacco and livestock remain farm products across the rolling terrain.
  • Beer cheese began here, and Winchester hosts a yearly festival for it.

How can I challenge a Clark County assessed value?

Phone the Clark County PVA at (859) 745-0250 and ask for a conference before the public review of the roll ends. The review lasts thirteen days from the first Monday of May, and a conference is the required first step. You may hold it by phone.

Still unhappy afterward? Put a written petition in the clerk's hands by the next workday after the review closes, naming the parcel, your reasons and your estimate of fair cash value. A hearing follows roughly a month later. The board expects facts, such as sale listings, construction costs or loan papers.

Officials can also start a review. The county judge/executive, a mayor or a school superintendent may ask the board in writing to look at specific parcels, which is how some values rise without the owner filing anything. The plain plan: confer, file, bring comparable sales and pay on the figure you claim.

How does the homestead exemption apply in Clark County?

An owner who has reached 65, or who is totally disabled, can have a set sum removed from the home's assessed value. The state figure was $49,100 for 2025 and 2026, and a fresh amount is published every second year. A home assessed at $210,000 would be taxed as though it were worth $160,900.

File with the Clark County PVA. A birth certificate, driver's license or passport shows age. Disability claims require a federal or retirement system classification, and most renew yearly.

What if I sell a Clark County house with unpaid tax?

Title companies pay the balance at the closing table out of your price. Ask the sheriff what the current bill stands at, and ask the clerk whether an earlier bill turned into a certificate of delinquency. Under KRS 134.015 the lien from an unpaid year stays with the land for eleven years whoever owns it, so a buyer's title search will turn it up.

Clearing the balance before April 15 is cheapest, because the sheriff holds the bill and extras stop at the penalty and add-on. Afterward the clerk's percentages stack up, and an outside investor can buy the claim. An empty, inherited or run-down house can still sell to an investor who accepts it unrepaired and pays the tax out of the price. Ask for that payoff to be shown as its own line on the settlement statement.

At closing, ask the agent to divide the current year by the date the deed transfers, so each side covers its own months.

Call the sheriff's office at (859) 744-4390 for bill and payment questions. For value questions call the Clark County PVA at (859) 745-0250.

When do Clark County bills get mailed?

Around October 1 each year. The 2025 notice said bills would go out September 30 and appear online, and that owners without a printed bill by October 15 should call.

Does the Clark County sheriff accept cash?

Yes, at the sheriff's office counter in Winchester. The downtown bank location listed in the 2025 notice does not accept cash.

Who sets the value of my Clark County home for tax?

The Clark County PVA, not the sheriff. The sheriff only collects the bill that results from the PVA's assessment and the local tax rates.

What if I miss the April 15 date in Clark County?

The unpaid bill transfers to the county clerk. There a 20 percent county attorney fee, a 10 percent clerk fee and 1 percent interest per month apply, and the bill can be sold to a third party.

By the time the sheriff transfers it, a 10 percent penalty, an add-on fee and an assumed 4 percent commission have lifted it to $1,254.00. Start at the PVA, because the state insists on a conference with the PVA or a deputy before an appeal is accepted. The real property roll is open for viewing for 13 days from the opening Monday of May, announced by the PVA in the paper with the biggest circulation.

Following the meeting, file with the county clerk no later than the next workday after viewing ends. A panel of local property owners then hears the case, between 25 and 35 days after viewing ends. Bring condition photos, repair estimates, insurance records and nearby sales. Evidence counts only if it is presented with you and the PVA's representative both present, and any change in value needs a written explanation.

You may make an audio recording of the hearing. If bills are printed while the case is pending, they use the value you gave. Should the board decide on a higher number, a supplemental bill makes up the difference.

How much tax does a typical Allen County house carry?

Kentucky's state real property rate for 2025 is 10.6 cents on each $100 of assessed value, lowered from 10.9 cents in 2024. For a house valued at the county's $192,300 Census median, the state's cut is about $203.84. Local levies sit on top of that figure, and the sheriff's tax bill search shows the full amount for any parcel.

An owner with the homestead exemption pays on $143,200 instead, which puts the state portion near $151.79. Neither number includes the 2 percent early-payment discount, which applies to the whole bill.

Who qualifies for the Kentucky homestead exemption in Allen County?

Owners at least 65 years old, and owners with a total disability classification, can claim it. The deduction is $49,100 across the 2025 and 2026 assessment years, taken from assessed value ahead of the rates. A house worth $192,300, the Census midpoint for Allen County, would be taxed on $143,200.

Send the application to the Allen County PVA, (270) 237-3711. Disability-based claims need yearly renewal. Two groups skip that step: veterans with a service-connected disability, and owners found permanently and totally disabled by Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems.

Allen County touches Tennessee and was carved out in 1815 from Barren and Warren counties. Scottsville is the seat and the only city. The Bowling Green metropolitan area includes the county, and bordering it are Warren, Barren, Monroe and Simpson counties in Kentucky plus Macon and Sumner counties in Tennessee. A fire at the courthouse in 1902 destroyed some county records, which can make very old title research harder. Land area is 344 square miles, and 77.5 percent of residents live in rural areas.

US 231, a four-lane parkway, links Scottsville to Interstate 65 about 30 miles away, and the county's own business page puts Nashville roughly 60 miles and Louisville 120 miles from town.

The population has been climbing. The 2020 census counted 20,588 residents and the latest federal estimate, for July 2025, is 22,536, a rise of 9.5 percent.

  • Housing units: 9,390 as of 2025.
  • Owner-occupied share: 74.5 percent.
  • Midpoint home value: $192,300.
  • Midpoint household income: $61,403, with 14.3 percent of people below the poverty line.
  • Mean commute: 27.3 minutes, against 23.8 minutes in neighboring Adair County.
  • Building permits issued in 2025: 17.

Households number 8,035, averaging 2.63 people, and 90.9 percent of residents stayed put over the previous year. The sheriff's office does more than collect: its county web page also lists enforcement of foreclosures, repossessions and tax delinquencies among its duties. Owner costs at the midpoint are $1,231 a month with a mortgage and $424 without, and gross rent at the midpoint is $844.

Permits totaled just 17 against more than 9,000 housing units, so resales dominate. A seller who has the tax account paid up and a clean deed of record faces fewer questions at closing.

More questions about Allen County, KY Property Tax Guide

Which Allen County office takes tax payments?

The sheriff does, as KRS 134.140 and 160.500 provide. The office at 194 W Wood St in Scottsville answers at (270) 237-3210. The PVA's role ends with valuation.

What is the penalty for paying Allen County taxes late?

Late payment costs 5 percent more in January and 10 percent more afterward. Once the bill reaches the clerk after April 15, monthly interest of 1 percent, commissions and fees join in, as the state's worked examples show.

Is the Allen County homestead exemption automatic at age 65?

No, you have to apply at the Allen County PVA. The state sets the figure at $49,100 for 2025 and 2026. Qualifying owners must be 65 or over, or totally disabled.

I bought a house in Allen County after January 1. Who gets the tax bill?

The seller's name appears on that year's bill, since ownership for tax purposes is fixed as of January 1. The PVA attempts to mail a copy to the buyer. If nothing comes, call the sheriff.

Can an Allen County tax lien block a sale?

It can slow one down. The lien stays on the parcel until the debt is paid or eleven years elapse under KRS 134.420, and a change of owner does not remove it. Obtain a payoff from the sheriff and clear it at or before closing.

What does Boyle County look like to a seller?

Boyle County fills 183 square miles of central Kentucky around Danville, the county seat. Junction City and Perryville are the other two cities. The county dates to 1842, carved from Lincoln and Mercer counties, and Perryville was the site of the October 8, 1862 battle. Centre College stands in Danville. Neighbors are Mercer, Garrard, Lincoln, Casey, Marion and Washington counties. Business figures for 2022 give the county economy some scale: $725.7 million in retail sales and $471.6 million in healthcare receipts.

Which school district bills Danville properties?

Street by street. Boyle County has two districts: Danville Schools inside the city and Boyle County Schools everywhere else. A handful of parcels inside the Danville limits still sit in the county district, so a Danville mailing address proves nothing.

Can I contest my Boyle County assessment?

A conference at the PVA's office comes first, and Kentucky offers no way around it. Values are fixed as of January 1. The roll lies open to the public for thirteen days in early May. After a conference you file the appeal with the county clerk by the close of the workday that follows the last open day.

The local board of assessment appeals sits roughly a month later, for up to five days. It wants evidence: nearby sales, an appraisal, repair quotes, insurance values or listings. Without it the appeal fails. An owner who never files locally cannot move on to the Kentucky Claims Commission.

Where bills are printed before the dispute ends, they use your own claimed value, with a supplemental bill if the board lands higher.

Who gets the Kentucky homestead exemption?

An owner aged 65 and up, or classed as totally disabled by a public or private retirement system, can knock a set dollar amount off the assessment of the home where they live. The state's ceiling is $49,100 through the 2026 tax year. Ownership and residence must both hold on January 1.

Applications go to the Boyle County PVA, which Danville names as the office for senior homestead questions. Send yours in before December 31. When your bill shows no exemption and you qualify, call the PVA before paying.

What happens when a Boyle County bill goes unpaid?

After April 15 the bill becomes a certificate of delinquency at the clerk's office and a lien attaches to the property. Interest accrues monthly at one percent, and clerk and county attorney commissions, postage and advertising pile on. The state's sample turns a $1,000 bill into $1,254 when it leaves the sheriff and roughly $1,388 within the first week at the clerk.

County attorney letters follow at about 30 and 60 days, and a sale of unpaid certificates to outside buyers can be set between 90 and 135 days after the handoff. A seller with old tax outstanding should ask the clerk for a payoff so the closing agent settles it from proceeds.

What happens to the tax bill when a Boyle County house sells?

Kentucky bills whoever holds title on January 1. A house that changes hands in March still produces that year's bill in the seller's name. Closing agents normally split the year between buyer and seller on the settlement statement, then either pay the sheriff or give a credit to the party who will. The PVA at 859-238-1104. The sheriff collects only, and the clerk handles appeal filings.

Is the Boyle County 2% discount still available after November?

No. On the 2026 bills the discount ran through November 30, 2026. December brings the face amount and January adds a 5 percent penalty.

Do Danville homeowners get one tax bill or two?

It varies. Parcels in the Danville Independent district get a separate school bill, while everything else, including Boyle County school tax, comes on the sheriff's bill.

The ceiling is $49,100 through the 2026 tax year, for owner-occupants aged 65 and up or totally disabled.

Yes. Ask the clerk for a payoff on past-due bills and the sheriff for the current figure, then have the closing agent pay both from proceeds.

Which Boyd County offices handle property tax?

Three do. The Property Valuation Administrator sets values. The Sheriff's Office bills and collects for the current year. The County Clerk picks up older delinquent bills.

The county's Property Valuation page says the PVA values all real and personal property in Boyd County, except items the Kentucky Department of Revenue assigns itself, such as public service companies, bank shares and vehicles. The PVA's mailing address is PO Box 434, Catlettsburg, KY 41129. For a house, the PVA's number is the starting point of everything else on the bill.

What is Boyd County's tax base like?

Land area is about 160 square miles, with roughly 300 residents per square mile, and 76.2% of people lived in urban areas at the 2020 count. The estimated 2025 population was 47,751 in about 21,818 housing units.

Boyd County's typical owner-occupied home is valued at $130,700 by the Census Bureau, and the typical household brings in $61,118. Owners live in 70.2% of homes. A house priced near that level carries a smaller assessment than most Bluegrass homes, yet the 911 fee and city levies still show up on the bill.

  • Ashland and Catlettsburg bill their own city property tax, and you call the city, not the county.
  • The county bill lists a 911 service fee, with questions going to Boyd County 911 at 606-329-2191.
  • Three school districts cover different parts of the county: Boyd County Public Schools, Ashland Independent and Fairview Independent.

When are Boyd County property taxes due?

The Sheriff's Office follows the calendar in KRS 134.015: a reward for paying early, a flat middle stretch and two steps of penalty.

Payment timingResult
By November 12% discount

The county's property tax page says online viewing and payment are available through the Sheriff's Office. Dates on a printed bill can run later than the statute's calendar when the state allows an alternative collection schedule, so read the bill and ask the sheriff's office which dates apply to your parcel. When the sheriff's collection period ends, unpaid prior year taxes move to the County Clerk, who handles them at 606-739-5116, option 4.

How do I contest a Boyd County assessment?

Go to the PVA first. The assessment date is January 1. When a property's value goes up from the prior year, the PVA mails the owner a notice of change.

The Boyd County PVA's appeals page explains the order of steps. Your first step is a conference with the PVA or a deputy. The window is six days a week for two weeks, starting the first Monday in May, though dates can shift. When the conference ends without agreement, a written petition to the County Clerk gets you a hearing before the board of assessment appeals, as KRS 133.120 provides.

  • Bring comparable sales, an appraisal, photos of damage or a contractor's repair estimate.
  • You may ask to hold the conference by phone.
  • The petition must give your reasons and your opinion of the property's fair cash value.
  • Keep paying while you appeal, since an appeal does not hold up the tax.

Does Boyd County have a homestead exemption?

Boyd County follows the statewide homestead exemption for owners who reach 65 or are classed as totally disabled. For the two years covering 2025 and 2026 the deduction is $49,100.

File with the Boyd County PVA. A birth certificate, driver's license or passport proves age. Disability claims need proof of a total-disability classification from a federal or retirement program. They are refiled yearly, except for veterans with service-connected disability and owners found permanently disabled.

What are the key dates in a Boyd County assessment year?

  • January 1: the assessment date for every property.
  • First Monday in May: the roll inspection period normally opens, and the PVA conferences begin.
  • Third Monday in May: the inspection period normally ends, and the written petition follows within a workday.
  • November 1: the last day for the 2% discount.
  • December 31: the last day to pay the plain face amount.
  • January 31: the last day before the 10% penalty.

The county's tax page posts a notice when each year's collection begins. Read the dates printed on your own bill, since the state can set an alternative schedule.

Who can speak for me in a Boyd County assessment appeal?

You can appear yourself, or you can use an agent. Kentucky law limits who may be paid to represent an owner at a PVA conference or a board hearing.

  • An attorney or a certified public accountant.
  • A tax consultant or a Kentucky licensed real estate broker or sales associate.
  • An employee of the property owner.
  • A licensed or certified Kentucky real property appraiser.

An agent carries written authorization from you and discloses any personal stake, such as a contingency fee. Losing at the county board leaves one more stop, the Kentucky Board of Tax Appeals, open only to owners who went to the county board first.

What does a late Boyd County payment cost on a sample bill?

Use a bill of $1,000 for illustration. Paid by November 1 it is $980. Paid from November 2 through December 31 it is $1,000. In January the 5% penalty brings it to $1,050, and after January 31 the 10% statutory penalty brings it to $1,100. Extra charges can attach after a bill moves to the clerk, so get a payoff figure from that office before closing.

These figures show the statute's calendar only. Your own bill carries the county, school and district amounts plus the 911 fee, and the Sheriff's Office can tell you the exact total for your parcel.

Call the Boyd County Clerk's office at 606-739-5116 and press option 4, or use the clerk's website.

Before the roll inspection window ends. The Boyd PVA says it normally opens the first Monday in May and closes the third Monday.

Where is Breckinridge County, and what is it like for homeowners?

Breckinridge County stretches along the Ohio River in western Kentucky, facing Perry County, Indiana. At 586 square miles, 567 of them land, it is the biggest of the four counties compared here. Hardinsburg is the seat and the largest city, with Cloverport and Irvington as the other two cities. Grayson, Ohio and Hancock counties adjoin it, and Meade and Hardin lie to the east.

The county was split from Hardin County in 1799 and was the 38th formed in Kentucky. Cloverport once shipped coal oil from the Victoria mines, and Rough River Dam State Resort Park opened up the southern edge in the 1950s. A local-option vote on January 29, 2013 ended 105 years of prohibition, making Breckinridge a wet county.

During the Civil War, Confederate cavalry burned the courthouse while Union troops were using it as a barracks, though most records were saved. Breckinridge County Public Library sits at 308 Old Highway 60 in Hardinsburg, and Saint Romuald Interparochial School is the private school.

Breckinridge runs on Central time, and the Meade and Hardin side to the east keeps Eastern time. A seller lining up a closing with offices across that line should confirm each office's clock.

What do the Census numbers show for Breckinridge housing?

The July 2025 estimate is 21,503 residents, 5.2 percent above the 2020 count of 20,432, which edges out Bullitt's 5.1 percent for fastest growth among the four. With 35.9 people per square mile, it is also the thinnest settled.

  • An owner's home has a middle value of $156,700 for 2020 to 2024.
  • Owners live in 81.4 percent of housing units, across 8,069 households.
  • Rent in the middle runs $733 a month, and monthly owner costs in the middle are $1,210 with a mortgage and $377 without one.
  • Household income in the middle is $55,843, and 18.3 percent of residents are below the poverty line.
  • Only 14 building permits were issued for 2025, against 10,952 housing units.

At the 2020 count about a quarter of the 10,704 housing units sat vacant, far above Bullitt's share. Few new homes compete with existing ones. Labor force participation among residents 16 and older is 52.6 percent, the average commute is 32.7 minutes, and 283 employers provided 2,480 jobs in 2023, down 0.8 percent from 2022. Retail sales for 2022 were $217.4 million, about $10,370 per resident, and the county counts 1,384 veterans. Broadband reaches 83.9 percent of households, a point to raise when buyers work remotely.

Which Breckinridge County office does what?

The sheriff bills and collects, the PVA values property, and the county clerk takes over unpaid bills. The Sheriff's Office is at 208 South Main Street, Suite 210, Hardinsburg, open weekdays eight to four Central. The phone is 270-756-2361 and the mailing box is PO Box 127. It collects about $11 million a year on behalf of the state, county, schools and special districts.

Assessment and homestead questions go to the PVA at 270-756-5154. Past-due real estate bills go to the County Clerk (270-756-2246), who quotes payoff amounts.

What are the Breckinridge County tax payment dates?

For the 2026 bills the sheriff said mailing would finish by October 29, and an owner without a bill by November 10 should ask for a duplicate. Online lookup and payment run from November 1 through 4 p.m. Central on April 15. Postmarks count.

Breckinridge County Sheriff's payment stages on the 2026 bills
WindowAmount owed

January 1 to 31Face amount plus 5%
February 1 to April 15Face amount plus 21%
After April 15Pay at the County Clerk's office

Statute and the Revenue Cabinet fix these dates and percentages, and the sheriff cannot bend them.

How does paying a Breckinridge County bill work?

The sheriff takes only the exact amount printed on the bill. A short payment is mailed back, and installments are not offered. One payment may cover several bills.

  • Online: a processing fee of 1.5 percent, minimum $1.50, applies on the first $60, and 2.5 percent on anything over $60. Visa, Mastercard, Discover and eCheck work.
  • Mail or counter: a check or money order with the voucher.
  • Fire dues: a signed opt-out form has to accompany the payment, so owners opting out pay by mail or at the counter.

Your cancelled check is the receipt, or enclose a stamped, addressed envelope for a mailed one.

How are taxes split when a Breckinridge County house sells?

The bill is made out to whoever owned on January 1. Selling after that date still leaves the bill in your name, and you pass it to the new owner. The closing agent usually allocates each side's portion on the settlement statement.

The sheriff will not accept two prorated checks. One party or the other has to pay the full bill, so ask the closing attorney who carries the payment and whether the buyer gets a credit.

How can a Breckinridge County owner dispute a valuation?

Values are set as of January 1, and the PVA's crews revisit every property about once in four years. If a new value seems wrong, schedule a conference with the PVA while the roll is open to inspection, which begins in early May and lasts thirteen days.

Only after that conference can you file with the county clerk, who serves as clerk to the local appeals board. The board meets about a month after inspection closes. Bring photos, a repair bid, an appraisal or comparable sales, since boards decide on paper and an appeal without it is denied.

Is there a senior or disability break in Breckinridge County?

Owners aged 65 and up, and owners classed as totally disabled, may claim the homestead exemption on the house they live in, up to $49,100 through the 2026 tax year. About 21.6 percent of residents are 65 or older, and 92.5 percent lived in the same house a year earlier. The sheriff sends every exemption question to the PVA, and says that checking for an exemption is the first move when a bill feels heavy.

What happens to unpaid Breckinridge County property tax?

The sheriff treats a bill as delinquent after April 15, or after the tax day assigned for that year, and extra penalties may apply. After April 15 the sheriff drops the bill and it shows up at the clerk as delinquent, with a lien on the property. Interest of 1 percent a month starts, commissions for the clerk and county attorney follow, and notices and advertising come before any sale. The Department of Revenue posts each county's delinquent list online by June 1, and on a normal schedule a sale can fall between July 14 and August 28. A third party can buy a bill that reaches the sale list. Anyone selling a house here with old tax owing should order the payoff before closing so the title company can pay it from the sale.

208 South Main Street, Suite 210, Hardinsburg, KY 40143. Payments by mail go to PO Box 127, and the phone is 270-756-2361.

Yes, starting November 1. A convenience fee applies, and the payment must equal the exact bill amount.

Can I pay Breckinridge County property tax in installments?

No. The sheriff accepts the full amount shown on the bill, though one payment can cover several bills.

When does the 21 percent penalty start in Breckinridge County?

On February 1, and it runs through April 15. After that the bill goes to the County Clerk as delinquent.

Who pays the tax on a Breckinridge County house I sold in June?

The January 1 owner is billed. The closing agent usually prorates the year, but the sheriff still needs the whole bill paid at once.

Which offices run property tax in Adair County, KY?

Adair County divides the job between two offices. One of them, the Property Valuation Administrator (PVA), assigns each parcel its worth, while the sheriff is the one who receives payment. The rate itself is voted by the bodies that levy the tax, such as the fiscal court and the school board.

Find the PVA on Public Square in Columbia: 424 Public Square, Suite 2, KY 42728, telephone (270) 384-3673, weekdays eight to four. Deputies there process deed transfers, including partial sales, and adjust vehicle values. On the same contact page the county lists the sheriff at (270) 384-2776 and the County Clerk at (270) 384-2801.

Kentucky freezes the picture on January 1: a parcel is appraised as it was that morning. Anyone closing in February will usually find the year's bill addressed to the seller, so the Adair County sale contract ought to spell out who repays whom.

When must Adair County tax bills be paid?

The sheriff takes payment through every stage of the statutory calendar in KRS 134.015. The table shows what each stage costs.

Adair County bill payment stages, statewide schedule (source: KRS 134.015)
Payment windowWhat you owe
On or before November 1Face amount less 2 percent
November 2 to December 31Face amount
January 1 to January 31Face amount plus 5 percent
After January 31Face amount plus 10 percent

If the state delays bill mailing, it may substitute a shifted calendar built on one-month blocks. Whatever remains unpaid at the end of the collection season, April 15 under the normal schedule, goes to the County Clerk with a recorded lien.

What would an Adair County owner actually pay?

Frankfort levies 10.6 cents for every $100 of assessed value in 2025, a cut from 10.9 cents in 2024. Put that against a $150,800 house, the Census midpoint for Adair County, and the state portion is roughly $159.85. Other taxing bodies add their own rates, so ask the PVA or the sheriff for the combined total on a given address.

The homestead exemption changes the math for older owners. If the assessment drops to $101,700 after the exemption, the state share falls to about $107.80. Paying early trims 2 percent off whatever the total turns out to be.

Those numbers matter in a sale because the year's bill has to be divided between buyer and seller somewhere. Ask the closing agent how the contract handles it, and ask the sheriff what has already been paid on the account.

How does an Adair County owner challenge a value?

An owner who wants to appeal must first confer with the PVA or a deputy. Public viewing of the roll starts on the first Monday in May and lasts through the following two weeks. Raise a disputed value then, or earlier if notices have already gone out.

  • The PVA is required to explain how your number was derived, and the meeting is documented in writing.
  • The appeal itself is filed at the County Clerk's office, with a deadline one workday after viewing wraps up.
  • Gather proof: descriptions of the land and buildings, insurance papers, building costs and comparable listings or sales. Without it the board turns the appeal down.
  • Attend the hearing, which comes a few weeks later. Filing and then not appearing forfeits later review by the Kentucky Claims Commission.

A paid representative has to fall into a listed category, for example an attorney, CPA, licensed broker or certified appraiser, and must bring your written authorization. If the board lands above the figure you claimed, you receive a supplemental bill for the gap.

Can an older Adair County owner reduce the tax base?

Yes, through the homestead exemption. People 65 and older, along with owners the law classes as totally disabled, receive a deduction that the state Revenue Department fixed at $49,100 for 2025 and 2026. Apply that to $150,800, the Census median home value here, and the taxed amount falls to $101,700.

File the form with the Adair County PVA during the year you want relief, by post, fax or email. The PVA accepts a driver's license, Medicare card or birth certificate as proof of age, with a Kentucky license or state ID covering residence. A household gets one exemption, and one spouse reaching 65 satisfies the age test.

Once approved, the exemption continues while the applicant stays in the home as owner. After a sale, the seller should notify the PVA so it is removed from the old address and can be requested for a new one.

What happens if I sell an Adair County house with taxes unpaid?

Selling does not erase an overdue balance. KRS 134.015 makes the tax the owner's own debt starting on the assessment date, and the parcel stays liened until payment or the expiry of the eleven-year span in KRS 134.420. A new deed does not change that. A title search will surface the lien, which is why the sheriff's payoff figure is worth getting before listing day.

While the County Clerk holds the account, each month adds 1 percent interest. The clerk and the county attorney take commissions, and a recording fee for the lien is added. Two notices go out by mail. Certificates can go on sale from 90 to 135 days after the handoff, and whoever buys one at that sale may add fees.

Paying the sheriff before April 15 avoids those clerk-stage extras completely.

What is Adair County, Kentucky, like for a seller?

Green County gave up part of its land in 1801 to create Adair County, whose lone municipality, Columbia, serves as seat. Roughly 405 square miles of land lie on the Pennyroyal Plateau, over 40 percent of it wooded. The Green River drains the county, and its impoundment as Green River Lake anchors a state park shared with Taylor County.

Farming drives the local economy: livestock, dairy, corn and tobacco. Road access improved a great deal once the Cumberland Parkway opened in 1973. Students attend Adair County Schools from the primary center to the high school. Census QuickFacts supplies these numbers:

  • 2025 population: 19,423, a gain of 2.8 percent over 2020.
  • Owner-occupied share of housing: 77.2 percent.
  • Home value at the midpoint: $150,800.
  • Household income at the midpoint is $53,553, and the poverty rate is 21.2 percent.
  • Gross rent at the midpoint: $771.

Neighbors on the map are Green, Taylor, Casey, Russell, Cumberland and Metcalfe counties. Columbia keeps Central time while Taylor and Casey counties to the north run on Eastern, a detail worth remembering when scheduling a closing with out-of-county parties. Rural areas hold 73.5 percent of the population, and the Census counted 7,136 households of 2.51 people on average.

The county recorded just six building permits in 2025, so nearly every sale involves a house that already stands. Where a house needs repairs or owes back taxes, selling for cash as-is lets both be cleared at a single closing.

More questions about Adair County, KY Property Tax Guide

When is the discount deadline for Adair County property taxes?

November 1 is the cutoff. Paying the whole bill by then saves 2 percent, the face amount applies from November 2 into December, and penalties start with the new year.

Who takes payment of Adair County tax bills?

Pay the Adair County Sheriff, whom the county lists at (270) 384-2776. The PVA, reachable at (270) 384-3673, only values property and never takes payments.

How much is the homestead exemption in Adair County?

The Department of Revenue fixed it at $49,100 for the 2025 and 2026 years, deducted from the assessed figure. Owners 65 or older, or totally disabled, apply at the PVA in Columbia.

Can I appeal my Adair County assessment after the deadline?

Not once the viewing period is over. The conference with the PVA must happen first, and the clerk filing is due the next workday after viewing ends. Viewing begins the first Monday of May and runs 13 days.

What happens if Adair County taxes go unpaid?

Once April 15 passes, the county clerk holds it as a certificate of delinquency backed by a recorded lien. Interest of 1 percent monthly accrues, and the certificate may be sold between 90 and 135 days after the handoff.

  • By mail: send the stub and a check to 701 Olive St., Murray, KY 42071, and add a stamped return envelope to get a receipt back.

  • Ask the clerk about any older delinquent year.
  • Check with the PVA that an exemption, if you have one, is on the account.

Speak with the PVA before anything else, then file with the clerk once the roll closes. Public inspection of the roll lasts 13 days from the first Monday in May, and a conference with the PVA must precede an appeal to the local board, per the state's property tax calendar.

Evidence decides these hearings. Expect the board to weigh land, buildings, rebuild cost and nearby sales. The state's sales comparison approach adjusts neighboring sales for differences like a basement, so collect three or four recent Murray sales and mark where your house differs.

An owner who files but fails to appear cannot take the case further, so attend with your paperwork. After the hearing the board must give a written reason for any increase or decrease, and you are allowed to make an audio recording.

Owners who live in the home and are 65 or older, or totally disabled, may apply for the homestead exemption. The sheriff's page tells anyone who might qualify to call the PVA at 270-753-3482 rather than pay first.

Only one exemption is allowed per household, and it belongs to the owner instead of the property, so your buyer files a new form. Service-connected totally disabled veterans do not refile each year.

Under Section 172A of the Kentucky Constitution, farm acreage is valued on what it can produce, not on market price. That gap can be wide near town, so anyone selling acres should ask the PVA how the parcel is classed.

A typical owner-occupied Calloway home is valued at $183,200 for 2020 to 2024, well over Caldwell County's $118,500. Owners live in just 63.9 percent of homes, and renters held 35.8 percent of occupied units in the 2020 count.

Household income in the county is $52,706 for 2020 to 2024, and 31.2 percent of adults hold a bachelor's degree or higher, against 17.1 percent in Caldwell County, a gap that fits a university town. Workers average 17.3 minutes getting to work, the shortest commute of the four counties in this group, so a house close to Murray's jobs and campus has a built-in appeal. The county makes up the Murray micropolitan area, and the 2020 Census put 15,108 households in it.

The county was created in 1822 from Hickman County, and a 1906 fire at the courthouse destroyed almost all of its early records, which is why old title questions sometimes need extra research. Yes, but the sheriff's page says credit cards are accepted only through its website. Cash, check and money order are also accepted, and cash should never go in the mail.

Who pays the bill if my Murray house sells mid-year?

Normally you pay a prorated share at closing and the buyer pays the full bill once issued. The settlement statement shows the split.

Must I fix up a Calloway County house first?

No, a cash buyer can take it as-is. Unpaid property tax is settled from the proceeds, so request payoff amounts from the sheriff and clerk first.

What makes property tax in Casey County, Kentucky different?

The yearly rhythm matches the rest of Kentucky: the PVA values property as of January 1, the sheriff collects from early October until April 15, and the county clerk picks up what remains. The difference is the setting. Casey County spreads over about 446 square miles with only one city, Liberty, and the 2020 census counted every resident as rural.

That shapes bills in practice. Almost every parcel is a farm tract, a hillside lot in the Knobs or a house on one of the state routes crossing the county, so the assessed value is the first number to examine before you list.

Which Casey County office handles which tax question?

Ask the PVA about value, the sheriff about what you owe this year, and the clerk about anything delinquent. The offices below are the ones the county's own pages list.

The clerk lists weekday hours of 8:00 am to 4:30 pm, except holidays.

What is the Casey County housing picture?

Small, spread out and mostly owned by the people who live in it. Lincoln County gave up its western portion to form Casey in 1806, and the courthouse in Liberty dates from 1888. The 2020 census recorded 15,941 residents in 6,270 households and 7,366 housing units, 14.9 percent of them vacant. Roughly 76 percent of occupied homes were owner-occupied, so many sellers are parting with the home they live in.

Wikipedia describes Casey as the only Kentucky county lying wholly in the Knobs, with its high point at Green River Knob, 1,789 feet. Hillside access, wells, septic systems and road frontage are worth documenting before you list. US 127, KY 80 and KY 49 are among the roads serving the county, and Casey County Schools operates the public schools. The annual Casey County Apple Festival is the county's signature event.

How do Casey County payment dates and penalties work?

The sheriff's bill sets the amount, and the payment date moves the total. KRS 134.015 gives a 2 percent discount for full payment through November 1, the bill amount from November 2 to December 31, a 5 percent penalty during January, and a 10 percent penalty starting February 1, with the sheriff's add-on fee on top.

The lien from an unpaid bill stays on the parcel for eleven years, whoever holds title. If collection starts late in a given year, the Department of Revenue can substitute a schedule that gives owners 30 days at each stage.

Lost the bill? Get the parcel number from the PVA or clerk and ask the sheriff for a copy. Mortgage escrow payments still leave the bill in your name, so confirm the payment posted before closing.

How can I contest a Casey County valuation?

Ask the Casey County PVA for a conference while the tax roll is open to public viewing, a thirteen-day stretch that starts the first Monday of May. A phone conference is allowed on request.

When that fails, mail or deliver a written petition to the county clerk by the workday after the viewing period ends, with the parcel, your reasons and your opinion of fair cash value. A hearing follows about a month later. Evidence carries the day: sales of similar houses, construction cost records, an insurance policy or a recent appraisal. Under KRS 133.120 the board denies an appeal if the owner will not hand over reasonable value information when asked.

  • Keep paying on the value you claimed while the case is pending.

How does the Casey County delinquent tax sale work?

After April 15 an unpaid bill goes to the clerk and can be sold to a private buyer at an annual sale. For the 2025 bills, the Casey County Clerk received the sheriff's list on April 16, 2026, ran the notice in The Casey County News on July 15, 2026, and set the sale for Friday, August 14, 2026 at 9:00 am in its office on Campbellsville Street. Those dates are behind us, and each year's sale follows a similar summer pattern.

Owners can pay up to the moment the sale opens. Bidders register with the clerk ten days ahead and pay a recording fee of $46 per lien assignment, as the clerk's page lists. Buying more than three certificates in a county, or more than five statewide, also requires registration with the Department of Revenue.

The sale itself runs like a draft. Registered buyers draw numbers at random, then take turns picking certificates from the lists they filed, and for the 2026 sale the clerk planned one certificate per round because of the volume. The clerk's office tells buyers it will not research bills for them, so a parcel with a problem such as a bankruptcy filing is the buyer's risk. Once someone buys your certificate, you owe that buyer and fees can grow. Paying earlier prevents it.

Does Casey County have tax relief for older or disabled owners?

Yes, through the state homestead exemption for owners in their retirement years or with a total disability. A fixed dollar amount comes off the home's assessed value. The Department of Revenue set it at $49,100 for 2025 and 2026 and publishes a new amount every second year. File with the Casey County PVA and bring proof such as a driver's license or passport.

The relief belongs to the owner who lives in the house. If you move into care or sell partway through the year, tell the PVA so the next bill reflects it.

How do I close a Casey County sale when tax is unpaid?

Collect written balances from the clerk and the sheriff and hand them to the closing agent. Anything unpaid at the table comes out of your price, and a lien the clerk filed must be released before the buyer takes clean title. Releases are recorded at the clerk's office for a posted fee.

For an inherited, empty or worn-down house, a cash buyer that takes the property as is can pay the tax from the price. That keeps your parcel off the August list, where delinquent bills become public.

Where do I find my Casey County property tax bill?

Ask the Casey County sheriff's office, which sends the bills. If you lack its number, the clerk at 606-787-6471 or the PVA at 606-787-7621 can point you to it and help identify your parcel.

When was the 2026 Casey County tax sale?

It was set for Friday, August 14, 2026 at 9:00 am at the clerk's office, 625 Campbellsville Street in Liberty. Owners could pay their unpaid 2025 bills up to the start of the sale.

How big is the homestead exemption for Casey County owners?

The state figure was $49,100 for 2025 and 2026, subtracted from the assessed value. It is open to owners 65 and up or totally disabled, and you apply through the Casey County PVA.

Is it too late to appeal if I missed the May viewing period?

Usually yes. The PVA conference and the clerk filing both fall inside that window, unless the state approved an extension of up to 25 days. Ask the PVA whether one applied.

Does unpaid tax stop me from selling Casey County land?

No. The bill and any lien get cleared at closing from your proceeds. Ask the sheriff or clerk for payoff amounts first so the title company can deduct them.

What should a Christian County, KY owner know about property tax?

At 724 square miles it is the second-largest Kentucky county by area and the largest in the west. Hopkinsville is the seat, and the other cities are Crofton, LaFayette, Oak Grove and Pembroke.

Settlers organized the county in 1797. The courthouse in use dates from 1869 and replaced one that Confederate cavalry burned in 1864 because Union troops were using it as barracks. The county runs on Central time and belongs to the Clarksville metropolitan area, with Montgomery and Stewart counties in Tennessee along its southern edge. Hopkins, Muhlenberg, Todd, Trigg and Caldwell counties share the Kentucky borders.

Who do I call in Christian County for each tax or records task?

Most of what a seller needs runs through the county clerk's office at 511 South Main Street in Hopkinsville, whose doors open at 8:00 am and close at 4:00 pm on weekdays. The clerk's own phone menu sorts the common tasks.

For the value of your house, contact the Christian County PVA. For the amount of this year's bill, contact the sheriff's tax office. If you cannot find a current number, ask the clerk's main line to direct you.

Half the occupied homes here are rented. The 2020 census counted 26,435 households and 29,206 housing units, with 49.9 percent owner-occupied and 50.1 percent renter-occupied. Median age was 30.0, 9.5 percent of units sat empty, and about 71 percent of people lived in areas the census calls urban.

Many sellers are therefore landlords. A landlord still owes the tax while a tenant lives in the unit, and an unpaid year follows the parcel into any sale. Christian County Public Schools serve most households, while Fort Campbell families are zoned to the federal DoDEA schools. Hopkinsville Community College and regional Murray State campuses are also here. The legal records division of the clerk keeps deeds back to 1797, which helps when a chain of title crosses several generations of owners.
